The John B. Hurford ’60 Center for the Arts and Humanities provides a place for inclusive and interdisciplinary programming by promoting collaborative engagement with the intellectual and artistic ambitions of Haverford College and broader communities.

News & Updates

M. Gessen Visits Haverford to Talk Autocrats and Hopeful Politics

The Pulitzer Prize winner visited campus for a wide-ranging conversation on autocracy, institutions, and what it takes to build something better.

Elsewhere, the Mountain: Hee Sook Kim and Landscapes of Belonging
Sep 4—Oct 9, 2026 Elsewhere, the Mountain: Hee Sook Kim and Landscapes of Belonging presents new and recent paintings by Hee Sook Kim that reimagine Mont Sainte-Victoire—an iconic motif in Western art history—through the visual language of Korean culture.
Amelia Lovelace '28 Carries Other People's Stories

The English and theater double major spent her summer developing new works at a Philadelphia theater company and then wrote a documentary play of her own.

Reworlding from Africa: Epistemic Justice, Relational Ethics, and the Planetary Turn
The 2026 Mellon Symposium, on Friday, February 20, organized by Ezgi Güner, is an invitation to rethink the world from Africa with the imperative to remake it: hence, reworlding from Africa
Citizenship as a Tool of Exclusion

A new book by Associate Professor of Anthropology Zainab Saleh explores how citizenship became a weapon in modern Iraq.

Raw Material: The Art and Life of Susan Kleckner

January 23—April 5, 2026 Raw Material: The Art and Life of Susan Kleckner is the first comprehensive survey of the pioneering feminist artist and filmmaker Susan Kleckner. Curated by William Kaizen.
